description: bravebot: a Rust workspace (cargo) with a thin npm wrapper, checked by ci.yml plus the organization-level brave/security-action scan.

judged.pr/risk/guarantee: The change can let untrusted content (text from the web, files or tools) decide something, give a value a better trust label than its inputs had, or reach the driver or the planner; or it changes what the trust map, permissions, routing, confinement or egress allow.
judged.pr/risk/network-calls: The change adds or alters a network request or destination: a new URL, host or fetcher, a change to what is sent, or a change to which server receives it.

checks: Whether the change agrees with the project's specs, and whether a change to behaviour a spec describes also updates that spec and its tests.
Whether untrusted content (text from the web, files or tools) can influence a decision, or be given a better trust label than it came with, anywhere other than the places built for that.
Whether the tests would fail if the behaviour broke, rather than covering only the allowed case or passing with the bug put back.
Whether the change does what its title says and nothing more, with no unrelated refactor and no new dependency, permission or network destination the title does not explain.
guidance: This review decides whether the bot recommends approving the pull request. Report what a maintainer would want fixed before approving, and nothing else.

Agreement with the specs. docs/specs/README.md lists every spec and the files it governs, and a spec wins where it and the code disagree. Read the specs that govern the changed files, and the specs the title concerns. Report a change that contradicts a clause, and a change to behaviour a clause states that leaves the clause and the tests it names unchanged. Never suggest rewording a clause to fit the code.

The untrusted-content rule, as docs/development/reviewing-for-the-rule.md states it. Report a branch on untrusted bytes, a `declassify` outside the policy gates, and a `Labelled` built by hand to give a value a better label than its inputs had.

Tests that can fail, per docs/best-practices/tests.md. Report a behaviour change whose tests cover only the allowed path, a relaxed assertion, and a test that would still pass with the fault restored.
Scope. Report a change that does nothing for what the title says, such as an unrelated refactor, and a new dependency, permission grant or network destination the title does not account for.
Report nothing that `make check` already decides: formatting, lints, clause numbering, lockfiles.
